content.text: Medieval logicians built on Aristotle. They worked out theories of meaning and of valid consequence.

content.definition: A theory of how a term in a sentence stands for things. The same word can stand for different things in different sentences.

examples.title: Three kinds of supposition
lines: 'Man is a species': man stands for the kind.
'Man has three letters': man stands for the word.
'A man runs': man stands for a person.

examples.title: Ockham's razor
lines: Do not multiply entities beyond need.
examples.note: Prefer the explanation that needs fewer things.

options: How terms in a sentence stand for things
question.hint: Look at the three kinds of supposition in the examples.
question.explanation: Supposition theory explained how a term stands for things. The same word can stand for the kind, the word, or a thing.
